subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: What public scheduler/config contract should OpenClaw use for foreground per-agent command lane isolation on shared gateways?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds public config and scheduler semantics that must settle lane ownership, aggregate caps, reserved lane names, and the request trust boundary before implementation.

options.title: Trusted per-agent lanes
options.body: Add a validated agent/defaults config surface that maps agents or groups to server-owned foreground lanes while keeping a separate aggregate safety cap.

options.title: Unified scheduler API
options.body: Defer this issue until foreground, subagent, hook, and workload-specific lanes can share one coordinated scheduler model.

options.title: Decline core surface
options.body: Keep the current shared main lane and document separate gateway processes as the supported isolation pattern for heavy agents.

recommendation.title: Trusted per-agent lanes
recommendation.body: Add a validated agent/defaults config surface that maps agents or groups to server-owned foreground lanes while keeping a separate aggregate safety cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail runs through the command-lane enum, gateway lane setup, and concurrency/default surfaces that define this scheduler contract.
